questions.q: In one study, how many of 24 healthy men showed brown-fat activity after 2 hours at 16 °C?
options: 23 of 24, and none at 22 °C
2 of 24
None, because adults carry no functional brown fat
questions.why: Biopsies confirm UCP1-positive brown fat in adults, and detection falls with age, BMI and summer.

questions.q: Why does a rise in plasma dopamine not show a rise in brain dopamine?
options: Plasma dopamine and brain dopamine are the same pool
The blood-brain barrier blocks and degrades circulating monoamines, and the gut makes close to half of body dopamine
All blood dopamine comes from the brain
The brain releases its dopamine into the blood within minutes
questions.why: That is why Parkinson's disease is treated with L-dopa rather than dopamine, and no human brain-dopamine study of cold water was found.

questions.q: How does cold water change plasma noradrenaline?
options: It rises about 10 % and stays high for a day
It rises 50-fold, far beyond anything exercise does
It rises 2- to 6-fold and returns to baseline about 30 minutes after rewarming
It does not change
questions.why: The rise sits inside the 1.5- to more than 20-fold range that exercise produces.

questions.q: What is the main acute danger of cold-water immersion?
options: Hypothermia within the first two minutes
Frostbite of the toes
A sudden fall in blood sugar
Cold shock in the first minutes: gasping, hyperventilation and a fast heart rate
questions.why: At 10 °C the first 30 s gave about 47 breaths/min, 68 L/min and 128 beats/min, while lean swimmers lost only 1.57 °C/h of core temperature at 16 °C.

questions.q: About how many short immersions habituate the cold-shock response?
options: About four
About forty
One
It never habituates
questions.why: Heart rate fell by a pooled 14 beats/min and ventilation by 21.3 L/min, but anxiety can reverse it and most of the tachycardia remains.

questions.q: What did breath-holding in 5 to 10 °C water do to the heart in healthy subjects?
options: It caused no change in heart rhythm
It produced ectopic arrhythmias in 29 of 36 submersions, mostly just after the breath-hold ended
It caused arrhythmias only in people with known heart disease
It gave a slower, more stable rhythm that protects the heart
questions.why: The proposed mechanism is an autonomic conflict between cold shock and the diving response.

questions.q: What happened to surgical patients held at 34.7 °C instead of 36.6 °C?
options: No difference in wound infections
Fewer wound infections in the cooler group
19 % against 6 % wound infections, and 2.6 more days in hospital
Half the hospital stay of the warmer group
questions.why: Hours of lowered core temperature impair infection defence; a plunge followed by rewarming is a different exposure.

questions.q: Against passive rest, what does cold water immersion after a hard session do to muscle soreness?
options: It removes soreness completely in high-quality trials
It increases soreness
It has no effect on soreness at any time point
It lowers soreness (SMD −0.55 at 24 h, −0.93 at 72 h), but the evidence is low quality
questions.why: The Cochrane review pooled 17 small trials with 366 participants, and strength recovery did not change significantly.

questions.q: What does cold water immersion straight after resistance training do to strength gains?
options: It reduces them by a small pooled effect (ES −0.23)
It doubles them
It increases them by a large effect
No trial has measured it
questions.why: Whole-body immersion alone was not significant (ES −0.08), and an umbrella review rated certainty low to very low.

questions.q: A leg cooled in 8 °C water for 20 minutes after lifting made how much myofibrillar protein over two weeks?
options: About 11 % more per day
About 11 % less per day than the leg at 30 °C
The same amount as the warm leg
Three times as much
questions.why: Synthesis was 1.48 against 1.67 %/day, and muscle blood volume was lower right after immersion.

questions.q: What does cold water immersion after endurance or interval training do to aerobic adaptation?
options: It doubles VO2max gains
It halves VO2max gains
It neither clearly harms nor clearly improves it
It blocks all mitochondrial adaptation
questions.why: The pooled effect for maximal aerobic power was SMD −0.07, with a confidence interval spanning both directions.

questions.q: How much heat did directly measured brown fat make during mild cold in people with the largest depots?
options: About 500 kcal a day
About 2,000 kcal per session
About half of all cold-induced heat
About 6.3 kcal a day, about 1 % of the extra heat the body makes
questions.why: Deep muscles are a major contributor to cold-induced heat, and muscle glucose uptake far exceeded brown-fat uptake.

questions.q: What does cold acclimation change?
options: Where heat comes from: shivering falls while total heat production stays the same
Total heat production, which doubles
Nothing at all, including shivering
Shivering, which rises 36 %
questions.why: Shivering fell 21 to 36 % after 7 days to 4 weeks with no net change in whole-body thermogenesis.

questions.q: What happened to food intake at the next meal after cold-water immersion?
options: People ate about 230 kcal less
People ate about 230 to 270 kcal more, more than the session burned
Intake did not change
People ate about 2,000 kcal more
questions.why: In 11 men, intake after cycling in 20 °C water was 44 % above that after neutral water.

questions.q: In the large trial of 30 to 90 seconds of cold at the end of a hot shower, what changed?
options: Illness days halved while absence did not change
Both absence and illness days rose
Self-reported sickness absence fell 29 %, but illness days did not change significantly
Laboratory-confirmed infections fell 29 %
questions.why: The 3,018-adult trial was unblinded, with self-reported outcomes and unverified compliance.

questions.q: In the endotoxin trial, what changed the inflammatory response?
options: Cold training alone
Neither cold nor breathing
Only the untrained control condition
The breathing technique, with cold plus breathing giving the largest effect
questions.why: Cold alone did not change the response (P = .77), the breathing did (P = .002), and the combination raised IL-10 44 % and lowered TNF-α 32 %.

questions.q: What does a cold-water plunge do to inflammatory markers?
options: It raises them for at least an hour
It lowers them immediately and they stay low
It leaves them unchanged
It raises them only after a week
questions.why: Pooled SMD was 1.03 immediately and 1.26 at one hour, and 10 minutes at 10 °C did not lower muscle inflammation compared with light cycling.

questions.q: What does a cold stimulus do to flow across coronary stenoses above 50 %?
options: It raises flow by 65 %
It cuts flow by 39 %
It leaves flow unchanged
It doubles flow
questions.why: The same test raised flow 65 % in normal arteries, and 22 °C water raised ventricular ectopy about fivefold in heart failure.

questions.q: How is outdoor temperature associated with heart-attack risk?
options: About a 20 % rise in risk per 1 °C fall
Lower risk in colder weather
About a 2.0 % rise in risk per 1 °C fall over the next 28 days
No association
questions.why: The rise concentrates in older and already-ill people, and it is weather evidence, not a test of plunging.

questions.q: What does hyperventilation before a cold breath-hold do?
options: It shortens breath-hold time and makes it safer
It prevents blackout
It has no effect on breath-hold time
It more than doubles breath-hold time and is the documented route to silent blackout
questions.why: In 58 underwater blackout cases after hyperventilation, 23 people died.

questions.q: Where does cold water clearly help exercise performance?
options: Pre-cooling before exercise in the heat (g = +0.53)
Before a sprint in cold weather
Before a strength test in a cool room
Ice slurry, which gave the largest effect
questions.why: Ice slurry showed no clear effect, and 15 minutes of cold water between two hot bouts prevented a 4.1 % fall in cycling work.

questions.q: How much do ten minutes at 10 °C cool the quadriceps?
options: The same amount at every depth
6.40 °C at 1 cm but only 1.61 °C at 3 cm
More at 3 cm than at 1 cm
Not at all at 1 cm
questions.why: Body fat percentage predicted cooling, and women cooled at about half the rate of men until fatness was matched.

questions.q: Which cooled deep leg muscle more: 10 minutes in 8 °C water or 2 minutes of −110 °C air?
options: The air, because it is colder
Both cooled the muscle by exactly the same amount
The water, 2.9 °C against 1.3 °C
Neither cooled the muscle
questions.why: Air conducts heat poorly, so a colder chamber cools the skin more but not the deeper tissue.

questions.q: What does the pooled evidence say about cold exposure and mood?
options: It proves cold cures depression
It proves cold worsens mood
Every randomised trial found a large mood benefit
It leans favourable but does not establish a benefit
questions.why: In 84 women, cold showers plus Wim Hof breathing and warm showers plus slow breathing both cut depressive symptoms 24 %.

questions.q: Where do the swimmers' mood and menopause benefits come from?
options: Self-selected surveys with no comparison group
Large placebo-controlled randomised trials
Hormone measurements in clinics
Brain-imaging studies
questions.why: 63.3 % of perimenopausal women swam to relieve the very symptoms they then rated.

questions.q: How did 34.7 °C water presented as a recovery treatment compare with 10.3 °C immersion?
options: It was much less effective
It was as effective
It caused injury
It was never tested
questions.why: Part of the felt recovery from an ice bath is expectation.

questions.q: Where did the +43 % insulin sensitivity result come from?
options: Thousands of healthy adults followed for a year
Brown fat alone in lean athletes
8 people with type 2 diabetes, through muscle, and it disappeared when shivering was prevented
A single 3-minute plunge
questions.why: Sixteen daily 10-minute plunges at 14 °C temporarily decreased insulin sensitivity.

questions.q: What does whole-body cryotherapy do in rheumatic disease?
options: It lowers CRP to normal with no change in pain
It worsens both pain and CRP
It cures rheumatoid arthritis
It improves pain without a consistent fall in CRP
questions.why: In RA, −130 °C cut pain by 1.31 NRS points versus control, and in ankylosing spondylitis CRP did not change.

questions.q: What followed brief foot chilling in the cold trial?
options: More self-reported colds, 13 of 90 against 5 of 90, without virological testing
Fewer colds after chilling
Laboratory-confirmed flu in half the chilled group
No colds in either group
questions.why: The result rests on 8 extra colds, and cell studies show that cooler airways weaken antiviral defences.

questions.q: What is the optimal temperature and duration for recovery immersion?
options: Exactly 11 °C for 11 minutes
None exists; the meta-analyses disagree on whether colder or shorter is better
0 °C for 30 minutes
15 °C for 2 minutes, proven best
questions.why: Recovery trials span about 5 to 15 °C for 2.5 to 15 minutes, and certainty is low to very low.

questions.q: What evidence supports ice for an acute soft-tissue injury?
options: Strong evidence that ice speeds healing
Strong human evidence that ice harms healing
22 RCTs with a mean PEDro score of 3.4 out of 10, and no human trial shows that ice speeds or harms healing
No trial has ever studied it
questions.why: The guideline favours supervised exercise, and PEACE and LOVE is an editorial, not a study.

questions.q: What is the +250 % dopamine figure?
options: A brain scan showing hours of raised dopamine
A large trial of daily cold showers
A mood study of winter swimmers
One plasma measurement during 1 hour at 14 °C that the same laboratory did not reproduce
questions.why: There was no brain measure, no mood outcome and no statement that levels stayed high for hours.

questions.q: What did three 4-week blocks of post-exercise immersion do to rugby players' fat mass?
options: Nothing; fat mass did not change
Fat mass fell 10 %
Fat mass rose
Fat mass halved while lean mass doubled
questions.why: No study has shown weight loss from cold-induced brown-fat activation.

questions.q: Where does the 11 minutes a week figure come from?
options: A randomised dose-finding trial
The self-reported mean weekly time of 7 or 8 Danish winter swimmers in a cross-sectional study
A public-health guideline
The dose that maximised fat loss in 1,000 adults
questions.why: The swimmers also took 57 minutes of sauna, and the study tested no dose.

questions.q: Why does the claim that cold boosts the immune system fail?
options: Laboratory-confirmed infections fell by half
White cell counts doubled for weeks
No study found measured laboratory-confirmed infections, and pooled immune markers showed no effect
Pooled immune markers showed a large boost
questions.why: Pooled markers gave SMD −0.16 immediately and −0.18 at one hour, from about 159 people.

questions.q: What did the Cochrane review find for whole-body cryotherapy?
options: 40 high-quality trials favouring chambers
That chambers cool muscle more than water
That chambers won every head-to-head trial
4 RCTs in 64 people with very low quality evidence
questions.why: A 13-RCT meta-analysis found cold water better for 24-hour soreness, and after a marathon chamber cold harmed muscle function compared with water.

questions.q: What is wrong with the claim that contrast therapy flushes lactic acid?
options: Lactate does not cause next-day soreness, and contrast clears it only slightly faster
Contrast removes all lactate instantly
Lactate is the main cause of next-day soreness
Contrast therapy raises lactate
questions.why: Downhill running caused soreness without a lactate rise, and active recovery near the lactate threshold clears lactate fastest.

questions.q: What did two hours at 10 °C do to testosterone in 20 men?
options: It doubled testosterone
Nothing; testosterone and LH were unchanged
It raised serum testosterone 21 %
It raised testosterone permanently
questions.why: Cold water after squats left testosterone 10.4 % below baseline at 60 minutes, and the one rise was salivary, not seen in serum in another trial.

questions.q: What is the Finnish HR 0.37 for sudden cardiac death?
options: A winter-swimming outcome trial
A Wim Hof breathing result
A sauna result with no cold-water exposure
A cold-shower cohort result
questions.why: No outcome study supports a heart benefit, and 15 days of daily Wim Hof Method changed no cardiovascular measure.

questions.q: What happens to measured cognition in cold of 10 °C or less?
options: It rises about 14 %
It does not change
It falls only for the first 10 seconds
It falls about 14 % and can stay impaired 60 minutes after rewarming
questions.why: Schedule skilled work before, not straight after, a long or very cold exposure.

questions.q: If muscle growth is your goal, how should you time cold exposure?
options: Keep it away from the minutes after lifting; a 4 to 6 hour gap is untested
Plunge immediately after every session
Wait 4 to 6 hours, a proven fix
Timing makes no difference
questions.why: Every training trial applied cold within minutes, and muscle perfusion stayed lower for 180 minutes after immersion.

questions.q: About how many extra kcal does a 3-minute plunge plausibly burn?
options: About 500 kcal
About 10 to 15 kcal
About 1,000 kcal
About 250 kcal, the same as the extra food eaten after
questions.why: That is less than the 230 to 270 kcal extra that people ate at the next meal after immersion.

questions.q: In the shower trial, how did 30 seconds of cold compare with 90 seconds for sick-leave days?
options: Only 90 seconds worked
Only 60 seconds worked
30 seconds performed as well as 90 seconds
Neither worked, but 10 minutes did
questions.why: The arms did not differ (P = 0.992), and a 15 °C shower does not cool the body the way immersion does.

questions.q: Does the time of day matter for cold-induced thermogenesis?
options: Yes: morning cold doubled it
Yes: evening cold abolished it
Yes: only fasted cold produced any
No: it was 16.8 % at 08:00 and 15.7 % at 18:00
questions.why: The crossover found no difference (P = 0.72), and evening post-exercise immersion left whole-night sleep unchanged.

questions.q: Why do people with cold urticaria need a medical assessment before regular plunging?
options: 37 % of test-positive patients had anaphylaxis, most often from full immersion
Cold urticaria only affects the hands
The only risk is mild itching
Cold water cures cold urticaria
questions.why: People with coronary disease, heart failure, a channelopathy or unexplained fainting also need an assessment first.
